results.blind_working: Distance from the 2 kg mass = (3 × 1.0)/(2 + 3) = 0.6 m.
No external force acts, so the centre of mass stays at the origin. Then 1(9) + 3x = 0, giving x = -3 m.
For a semicircular wire the centre of mass is 2R/π from the centre: 2(11)/(22/7) = 7 cm.
A is true: the ring's centre of mass is at its geometric centre, where there is no material. R is also true, but it concerns centre of gravity and does not explain A.
Solid hemisphere: 3R/8. Hollow hemisphere: R/2 = 4R/8. They differ by R/8, so I is correct. The explosion forces are internal, so the centre of mass keeps following the parabola; II is incorrect.
From rest, θ = ½αt² = ½ × 2 × 5² = 25 rad.
Tangential acceleration a_t = αr = 3 m/s². Centripetal acceleration a_c = ω²r = 4 m/s². They are perpendicular, so a = √(3² + 4²) = 5 m/s².
All particles of a rigid body share the same ω. Since v = ωr, Q at 2r has twice P's linear speed.
Tangential acceleration is αr (II). Centripetal acceleration is ω²r (I). Linear velocity is ω×r (IV). Angular displacement is ω₀t + ½αt² (III).

A is true: all particles share the same angular displacement. B is false: ω lies along the axis, not in the plane of rotation. C is true: tangential and centripetal accelerations are perpendicular. D is true: rolling is translation of the centre of mass plus rotation about it. E is false: a particle on the axis has zero speed. So A, C and D.
The torque is τ = rF sinθ = 0.5 × 20 × sin30° = 5 N m.
The torque is τ = r × F. Its z-component is (2)(1) − (3)(4) = −10, so τ = −10k̂ N m.
The two forces form a couple, and a couple's torque is the same about any point. About a point on one line, only the other force contributes: τ = 10 × 0.3 = 3 N m.

A force whose line passes through the axis has zero perpendicular distance, so its torque is zero. A is false. R correctly defines torque magnitude as force times perpendicular distance, so R is true.
Torque is a vector despite having the same dimensions as work, so Statement I is false. A couple's torque does not depend on the reference point, so Statement II is false.
Angular momentum is conserved: I1ω1 = I2ω2, so ω2 = (6×2)/2 = 6 rad/s.
L = 4×3 = 12 kg m²/s. Final ω = 12/2 = 6 rad/s. KE = ½×2×6² = 36 J.
L = m v d, where d is the perpendicular distance from the origin to the line of motion (4 m). L = 2×3×4 = 24 kg m²/s.

A: L is conserved and I decreases, so ω and KE both increase (I). B: Kepler's second law, areal velocity constant (II). C: the disc's centre of mass is at rest, so net linear momentum is zero and L is the same about every point (III). D: L = mvd is constant about any fixed point (IV).

A true. B false: stretching the arms increases I, and KE = L²/2I decreases. C true: a central force passes through the centre, so its torque is zero. D true: τ = dL/dt. E false: the skater's KE increases.
I = Σmr² depends on mass, its distribution and the axis, but not on angular velocity.
A is true: rim mass gives a large I for storing rotational energy. R is true but does not explain the design.
I is false: k depends on the axis. II: ring k = R; sphere k = R'√(2/5). Setting R = R'√(2/5) gives R'/R = √(5/2), so II is true.
Moments of inertia: sphere 2/5 MR², disc 1/2 MR², shell 2/3 MR², ring MR². The ring is largest.
I = ML²/3 = 3×4/3 = 4 kg m².
About the symmetry axis, length does not matter, so I = MR²/2.
Ring about a diameter is 1/2 MR² (II). Disc is 1/4 (I). Shell is 2/3 (IV). Solid sphere is 2/5 (III).
A is true. B is true. C is false because 2/5 < 1/2. D is false because a hollow cylinder has MR². E is true because ML²/3 = 4 × ML²/12.
I_cm = ML^2/12 = 3*16/12 = 4; parallel axis adds Md^2 = 3*1 = 3; total 7 kg m^2
Two diagonals are perpendicular in the plane and have equal I; their sum is I_z = Ma^2/6, so each diagonal gives Ma^2/12
Since I = I_cm + Md^2 >= I_cm, A is true. The theorem requires one axis through the CM, so R is false

I is false: the perpendicular axis theorem applies only to planar bodies, and a sphere about a diameter has I = (2/5)MR^2. II is true: tangent perpendicular to plane gives 2MR^2; tangent in plane gives (3/2)MR^2; ratio = 4/3
A couple gives zero net force, so the body is in translational equilibrium. Its torque is non-zero, so it is not in rotational equilibrium.
Taking moments about the fulcrum: E × 1.2 = 600 × 0.2, so E = 120/1.2 = 100 N.
Taking moments about B: R_A × 4 = 400 × 3 + 200 × 2 = 1600, so R_A = 400 N.

A couple gives translational but not rotational equilibrium (A-IV). A suspended body at rest has its CG directly below the suspension point (B-I). A longer effort arm gives MA > 1 (C-III). Zero net force plus zero torque about one point means zero torque about every point (D-II).
A is true. B is false, since a couple is a counterexample. C is true. D is false, because a longer effort arm gives MA > 1. E is false. So the correct statements are A and C only.
For rolling without slipping, KE = (1/2)mv²(1 + K²/R²). For a disc K²/R² = 1/2, so KE = 0.5·2·9·1.5 = 13.5 J.

A is true: static friction acts at the instantaneous contact point, which is at rest, so it does no work and energy is conserved. R is true: friction is needed to provide the torque for rolling. R does not explain why energy is conserved; the zero work done by friction does.

I is correct: a = g sinθ/(1 + K²/R²), independent of mass and radius, and the sphere (K²/R² = 2/5) beats the ring (1). II is incorrect: with no friction both slide with a = g sinθ and arrive together.
Linear momentum p = mv maps to angular momentum L = Iω, with m→I and v→ω.
Angular impulse τt = 12 = Iω, so ω = 12/2 = 6 rad/s.
Force→torque (III), mass→moment of inertia (IV), momentum→angular momentum (I), power Fv→τω (II).
A is false because I depends on the axis. B, C and D are true. E is false because τω is power, not work.
